newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: S.Africa requests extradition of Zimbabweans.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa requests extradition of Zimbabweans.

text.p: South Africa has asked Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe to release into its custody five Zimbabweans serving life jail terms for offences linked to an apartheid-era sabotage campaign, it was reported on Thursday.

"President (Nelson) Mandela put that request to President Mugabe during their talks this week. I hope the request will receive favourable response," South African Foreign Affairs Minister Alfred Nzo told the Financial Gazette newspaper.

Kevin Woods, Philip Conjwayo, Michael Smith and Barry Bawden were arrested a decade ago for a spate of bombings at several African National Congress houses in Zimbabwe when South Africa's now-ruling party was still outlawed. Another man, Dennis Beaham, was jailed for trying to free the four from prison.

Mandela's government says the five, granted South African citizenship by the Pretoria government soon after their arrests, should be freed in line with a general amnesty the ANC proclaimed when it assumed power in 1994.
Nzo said the men were also needed to testify to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission set up to investigate apartheid-era crimes and heal the wounds of the past.

Zimbabwean officials were unavailable for comment but Mugabe's government has been adamant that the prisoners would not be released since they were Zimbabweans and had committed the crimes in the country.
Their families have held picket protests in South Africa and petitioned the government to help secure their return.
